title: Potentiometer -> RGB Color
summary: In Lesson 4, you discovered that an RGB LED contains three microscopic diodes (Red, Green, Blue) packaged inside a single lens.

steps.title: Potentiometer -> RGB Color

quickCheck.question: What type of Arduino pins must you connect to an RGB LED's color channels to mix custom colors?
options: PWM pins designated with a tilde ~ (such as 9, 10, 11)
Analog input pins A0 through A5 only
Only the 5V power and Reset pins
quickCheck.explanation: PWM pins provide variable duty cycles via `analogWrite()`, enabling color mixing on RGB LEDs.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: RGB color mixing requires PWM output pins to adjust the individual brightness of each color channel.

quickCheck.question: How can a continuous potentiometer reading (0 to 1023) select between four distinct robot modes?
options: By dividing the 0-1023 range into four numeric threshold zones in code
By rotating the knob faster than 500 RPM
By toggling the computer's USB port
quickCheck.explanation: Threshold intervals in code allow a continuous analog signal to select discrete operating states or colors.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Code can divide numeric ranges into discrete buckets using `if-else` threshold comparisons.

questions.question: How can a single rotary knob select among multiple colors?
options: Divide the 0-1023 reading into ranges using IF/ELSE checks or math equations
questions.explanation: Splitting the 0-1023 range into segments lets one knob select presets or blend colors!

questions.question: What visual component helps learners verify sensor readings in real time?

questions.explanation: The Serial Monitor and Plotter show live numerical graphs of potentiometer movements!
